title: Photoroom Pricing: All Plans and Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Photoroom pricing includes a free tier and multiple paid plans. Compare features and costs to decide which plan matches your editing needs and budget.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits Photoroom users hit


On the chart, the per-image cost assumes every image you export is usable and billed to one place, and five things break that:


- the Free watermark
- the export cap
- separate API credits
- the billing channel
- renewal terms


### Free plan watermark and export limits


Because Free exports carry a watermark, they work for testing the cutout quality but not for a live product listing.


If you publish them anyway, the real cost is reshooting or reprocessing the same images on a paid plan, which **means paying twice for each one** .


Treat the Free allowance as a trial budget, not a production tier.


Exports pause until the next billing cycle once you reach a paid plan's ceiling. A cap that stops you mid-batch costs you a stalled catalogue, and the fix is either waiting or upgrading early. Count your busiest month, not your average one.


### App subscription versus API billing


**Two purchases, not one** : the app plan and the API are billed separately. API credits are billed apart from the app subscription, so a paid app plan doesn't cover images you send through code.


If you run an automated pipeline, you pay for the plan your team uses in the editor and the credits your scripts consume.


That split matters when comparing alternatives. A rival priced as one metered API line isn't comparable to Photoroom's app price alone. Add the credit spend to the plan fee before dividing by image count.


### Photoroom seat costs, batch limits and renewals


A plan that looks cheap for one designer grows with every colleague who needs access, because team plans add cost per person. Check whether the people who only review images need a seat at all.


Batch limits also matter. A cap on how many images process at once turns one job into several, which costs time even when it costs no money.


**Where you subscribe changes the bill too** . App-store subscriptions and web subscriptions are billed and managed in different places, and prices can differ between them. **Cancelling in one place doesn't cancel the other.**


Before you commit, confirm which channel holds the subscription, when it renews, and where you cancel. Check the renewal terms on the checkout page itself, and if you can't find them without contacting sales, count that against the plan.


> **Cancelling in one place doesn't cancel the other.
